text:
### Observed differences

- A01 and A08 exchanged presence: A01 appeared in 96 of 200 traces before (about 48 in 100) and in none of the 200 later traces, while A08 appeared in none before and in 96 of 200 later traces. Both occur about twice in the traces that contain them and sit around 55–57% of the way through the trace. [OCC001, OCC006, POS001, POS008]
- A08 also took over A01's connections. Before, A01's outgoing transitions went to A09 (about 51%), A10 (about 24%) and A16 (about 24%); in the later window A08's outgoing transitions go to the same activities in similar shares (A09 about 56%, A10 about 25%, A16 about 19%). A17, which previously always led to A01, now always leads to A08, and the hand-offs from A03 that went to A01 (about 21% of A03's outgoing transitions) now go to A08 (about 26%). [DIR001, DIR006, DIR012, DIR003]
- Co-occurrence moved the same way: A08 now appears together with A02 and with A03 in about 48 in 100 traces each, the shares A01 had before, and A08 never appears together with A15 — exactly one of the two is present in every later trace, mirroring the earlier mutual exclusivity of A01 and A11 (about 48 vs about 52 in 100, never together). [REL001, REL002, REL023, REL037, REL103, REL010]
- A11 and A15 exchanged roles. Before, A11 was the closing activity: present in 104 of 200 traces (about 52 in 100), always the final event, with no observed outgoing transitions, while A15 appeared in 64 of 200 (about 32 in 100) around mid-trace (mean position about 0.49) and all of its observed outgoing transitions led to A03. In the later window the roles are reversed: A15 is present in 104 of 200 traces, always the final event, always after A02, with no observed outgoing transitions, while A11 appears in 58 of 200 (about 29 in 100) at mid-position (about 0.54) and all of its observed outgoing transitions now lead to A03. A05's transitions that previously went to A11 (about 52%) now go to A15 (about 52%), and A18's transitions that went to A15 (about 21%) now go to A11 (about 26%). [OCC009, OCC011, POS011, POS014, DIR005, DIR008, DIR010, DIR013, REL026, REL029]
- Event distances agree with this exchange: A04 to A11 was always five positions apart before and is most often two after, while A04 to A15 was most often two before and is always five after; A18 to A11 moved from always four to most often one, and A18 to A15 from most often one to always four (event positions, not clock time). [LAG035, LAG036, LAG077, LAG078]
- Smaller shifts outside these two changes: the A04/A18 pair, which always occurs together, now repeats less often (mean about 2.2 down to about 1.6 occurrences per trace), and A07 participates in fewer traces (about 38 in 100 before, about 27 in 100 after). [OCC003, OCC014, OCC005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that in the later window A08 has taken over the role previously played by A01: A01 was observed in about 48 in 100 traces before and in none after, A08 in none before and about 48 in 100 after, and A08 matches A01 in participation, mid-trace position, successors (A09, A10, A16), predecessor (A17, whose only observed outgoing edge switched from A01 to A08) and co-occurrence shares with A02 and A03. Occurrence, direction, position and relation indicators all show this transfer directly, and differences of this size were virtually never produced by random re-splits of the two windows. The main limitation is that a genuine replacement of A01 by A08 cannot be distinguished from the same behaviour being recorded under a new activity code. [OCC001, OCC006, DIR001, DIR006, DIR012, POS001, POS008, REL007, REL023, REL037]

Other differences: A11 and A15 exchanged their roles — A15 became the closing activity (about 52 in 100 traces, always last, following A02, no observed outgoing transitions), the role A11 held before, while A11 moved to a mid-trace position (about 29 in 100 traces) and now leads to A03, the role A15 held before; direction, position, relation and lag evidence agree on this exchange. In addition, the A04/A18 pair repeats less often and A07 participates less often. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that these exchanges reflect renamed rather than rewired activities, since the activity codes are anonymous and the evidence contains no clock-time or resource items to corroborate either reading. [OCC009, OCC011, POS011, POS014, DIR005, DIR008, DIR010, DIR013, REL026, REL029, LAG036, LAG078, OCC003, OCC005]
